title: Transitous
description: Worldwide public transport search and journey planning over Transitous, the community-run MOTIS instance. Attach to a route whose upstream is https://api.transitous.org/api. No credential is needed.
instructions:
Start with transitous_search_place. Everything else takes a place or stop id that only a search returns, and those ids are opaque, so never construct one. A 'lat,lng' string also works where an id is asked for.

REAL TIME IS PATCHY. Every leg and stop time carries a realTime boolean. True means the times are live-adjusted, so compare against the scheduled fields and report the delay. False means they are timetable only: say so, and never present that as 'on time', because nothing observed it. Always surface cancelled and tripCancelled. Showing a cancelled connection as usable is the worst thing this bridge can do.

Coverage is whatever feeds the community has imported, broad in Europe and patchy elsewhere. A place that returns nothing is usually a coverage gap rather than a bad query, and saying so beats trying five spellings.

Times are ISO 8601 with an offset. Journey planning is real time and is not cached, so the same call a minute later can legitimately differ.

This is volunteer-hosted and non-commercial. Do not poll it, do not fan one question into a dozen calls, and credit the data: Transitous (https://transitous.org/sources/) and OpenStreetMap contributors. Put your own contact address in the User-Agent below, replacing the placeholder, so the operators can reach whoever is making the requests.

tools.name: transitous_search_place
tools.title: Find a place or stop
tools.description: Searches stops, stations, and addresses by name and returns their ids, coordinates, and which transport modes serve them. Always the first call: every other tool here needs an id from it.

text.description: What to look for, e.g. 'Zürich HB' or 'Alexanderplatz Berlin'.

tools.name: transitous_plan_journey
tools.title: Plan a journey
tools.description: Journeys between two places, with legs, changes, and times. Origin and destination are ids from transitous_search_place, or 'lat,lng' strings. Returns an itineraryId that transitous_refresh can update later.

time.description: ISO 8601 with offset. Omit for now.

arriveBy.description: True to treat time as 'arrive by' rather than 'depart at'.

transitModes.description: Comma separated, e.g. 'RAIL,BUS'. Omit for every mode.

tools.name: transitous_departures
tools.title: Departures or arrivals at a stop
tools.description: The next services calling at one stop, with real-time times where the feed provides them. stopId comes from transitous_search_place. Set arriveBy true for arrivals instead of departures.

n.description: Roughly how many events to return.

arriveBy.description: True for arrivals, false or omitted for departures.

mode.description: Comma separated modes to filter by, e.g. 'RAIL,BUS'.

tools.name: transitous_refresh
tools.title: Re-check a planned journey
tools.description: Takes an itineraryId from a previous transitous_plan_journey and returns it with current real-time data. Use this instead of planning the same journey again when the user asks whether it is still on time.

itineraryId.description: From the itinerary returned by transitous_plan_journey.

tools.name: transitous_health
tools.title: Service health
tools.description: Whether the Transitous instance is up and how current its feed data is. Worth one call when journeys look wrong or empty, to tell a coverage gap from an outage.

skills.name: transitous-obligations
skills.title: Using a volunteer service properly
skills.description: What stands in for an API key here, and how to read real-time flags.
skills.content:
# Transitous, honestly

## There is no key, and that is the point

The public endpoint is volunteer-hosted and unauthenticated. What stands in for a key is behaviour: an identifying User-Agent with a contact address, attribution on anything you show, restraint in how often you call, and non-commercial use. If this becomes work, self-host MOTIS rather than leaning on the public instance.

## Reading real-time flags

| `realTime` | What it means | How to label it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `true` | live-adjusted times | compare with the `scheduled*` fields and state the delay |
| `false` | timetable only | say the times are scheduled, not observed |

Never turn `realTime: false` into 'no delay'. Nothing measured it. Coverage is good on major urban and long-distance services and thin on rural ones.

## Cancellations

`cancelled` on a leg and `tripCancelled` on a trip must always reach the user, even when the rest of the itinerary looks fine. A cancelled connection presented as valid is the failure that strands someone.

## Attribution

Data: Transitous (https://transitous.org/sources/) and OpenStreetMap contributors (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright).
